title: Beyond exons: Linking noncoding heritability and polygenicity across complex human traits and disorders.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: paper_context.py: no PMCID for the AJHG version, no supplement, no accessions, no NCBI or Zenodo/Dryad links. Read the bioRxiv preprint mirrored in PMC (PMC13060159): its code statement is a placeholder ('XXX.zip, made public upon publication'), and its only supplement is one 2.1 MB PDF (media-1.pdf) holding Tables S1 and S2.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 34 traits (pruned from 70 public European-ancestry GWAS, i.e. genome-wide association studies) × 74 functional annotations; heritability fractions and annotation contribution scores estimated with MiXeR. I did not open the PDF tables or any GWAS summary statistics.

a1_downloadable.note: AJHG version is paywalled with no supplement retrievable. The preprint's results sit only in PDF tables, and its code link is a placeholder. Not checked in files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No label table exists. Any target (per-trait heritability fraction per annotation) would have to be rebuilt by re-running MiXeR on GWAS summary statistics.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs would be GWAS summary statistics fetched one by one from many public consortia (listed in Table S2 per the paper), not present here.

a4_units_stated.note: Heritability fractions are proportions, per the paper text; not checked in files.

a5_enough_rows.note: The real unit is the trait: 34 traits (paper text). Even 34×74 = 2,516 trait-annotation cells are not independent examples.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown; the PDF tables are small, but rerunning MiXeR on 70 GWAS is heavy

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No downloadable table to count against. The preprint analyses 70 phenotypes, reduced to 34 after pruning (paper text).

a8_label_provenance.note: Any label would be a statistical model's estimate (MiXeR partitioned heritability), not a direct measurement, so the project would distil that model.

honest_claim_h3: With 34 traits, a model could at most describe how MiXeR-estimated annotation heritability fractions change with polygenicity in European-ancestry GWAS; that is a correlation, not a prediction task.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a trait's polygenicity and genome annotations to predict how much of its heritability sits in each genomic region type.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-trait polygenicity estimates and 74 annotation categories; 34 traits (paper text, not verified).
plain_idea.predict: The fraction of heritability from each annotation, estimated by the MiXeR statistical model from GWAS summary statistics, not measured directly.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Statistical geneticists choosing where to look for causal variants might use it, but 34 traits is too few to learn anything beyond what the paper already reports.

label_elsewhere.sources: Partitioned heritability from S-LDSC (stratified linkage-disequilibrium score regression) appears in many published papers (known method); not searched as a joinable resource.
label_elsewhere.why: Not filled in depth because the verdict is reject.

ml_idea: None viable: this is a statistical-genetics analysis of 34 traits with model-derived outputs, not a dataset for ML.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; rejected at Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the units: 34 traits, which already kills it.

verdict_reason: Analysis paper, not a dataset. The unit is 34 traits, the only outputs are MiXeR model estimates in PDF tables, the AJHG version is paywalled, and no code or data has been deposited. Fails A1, A2, A5 and A8.
